clue.text: I'd recalled tucking into impulsive item for salad

indicators.note: tucking one thing into another places it inside, so the turned letters sit within the synonym

parts.note: an impulsive act is a rash one

indicators.note: recalled in the sense of called back, so the letters of I'd are read in reverse order

parts.note: I'd contributes its two letters

explanation.surface: Someone remembers sneaking a rash, spur-of-the-moment ingredient into a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' means called back, so I'd is turned round before it is tucked inside the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppery red root vegetable, this is a standard component sliced into salads.

clue.text: Live on edge

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a side is an edge or margin of something

explanation.surface: An instruction or description: living life on the edge, dangerously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' reads as the adjective or the 'live on' of living dangerously; it is the verb meaning to dwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to dwell or have one's home somewhere is to live there.

clue.text: Lorna's accepted temptation to make a contribution

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so her possessive gives DOONE'S
a fish that accepted the lure or bait is said to have bit

explanation.surface: A woman named Lorna gave in to temptation in order to contribute something.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorna Doone is the title heroine of a classic English romantic novel set on Exmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for playing one's part or contributing a fair share to a common effort.

clue.text: Fuel vessel in hurry

definitions.meaning: a coal container kept by the fireplace
to scurry or run with short quick steps

explanation.surface: A tanker or fuel ship being rushed along.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a coal bucket by the hearth, and the verb for scampering off quickly.

clue.text: Rough strikebreaker's going to stir endlessly

parts.note: a scab is a worker who crosses a picket line

indicators.note: endlessly means the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: to rouse is to stir or wake up

explanation.surface: A rough-mannered strikebreaker is about to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final E from ROUSE; the 's (is) and 'going to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a surface that is scaly or harsh to the touch, hence rough.

clue.text: Bring into church, with introduction of Irishman, this old Tory

indicators.note: introduction here means something being put in, so the name goes into the middle of the verb

parts.note: to christen a baby is to baptise it and so bring it into the church
Pat (Patrick) is the stock crossword Irishman

explanation.surface: A former Conservative politician is ushered into church alongside an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring into church' means baptise, not escort. He was Conservative Party chairman and the last British Governor of Hong Kong.
explanation.definitionFit: A former Conservative cabinet minister and party chairman, now retired from frontline politics.

clue.text: Crazy about the Queen's source of power

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the mad word goes round the royal letters

parts.note: batty is informal for crazy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: Someone is madly enthusiastic about where the monarch gets her energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell or set of cells that stores electrical charge supplies power to a device.

clue.text: Different article carried by soldiers

indicators.note: carried by means held within, so the article sits inside the soldiers

parts.note: OR, ... ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A distinct piece of kit is being carried by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something distinct or not the same as the one mentioned.

clue.text: Is artist playing Ravi Shankar?

definitions.note: a proper name defining a class of performer by example

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being played around with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question asking whether the artist on stage is Ravi Shankar himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like a performer at work but signals the anagram; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravi Shankar was the most famous Indian player of the long-necked stringed instrument, an example of the type.

clue.text: Japanese ruler removing central element of firearm

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter gun is taken away

parts.note: a shotgun is a firearm firing pellets

explanation.surface: A Japanese warlord is taking out the key part of a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourth of seven letters, T, is the centre removed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereditary military commander who effectively governed feudal Japan for centuries.

clue.text: Note hobby that gets one hooked takes time

indicators.note: takes means the hobby swallows up the time letter inside itself

parts.note: crochet is needlework done with a hook, and an addictive pastime

explanation.surface: Someone observes that an addictive pastime eats up hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooked' puns on crochet's hook and on addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note worth one beat, the quarter note in American terms.

clue.text: Detective arresting the old thugs, reportedly showing colours

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the detective's letters go round the old word

parts.note: DS is a Detective Sergeant
ye is an old form of the

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, spelt by its sound

parts.note: toughs are thugs or hoodlums

explanation.surface: A police officer is arresting some old-time thugs who flaunt their gang colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' applies only to the thugs; 'showing' is a link word, and 'colours' reads as gang insignia but means pigments.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyes and pigments are substances that give colour, here the colours themselves.

clue.text: Healthy knight on board's speciality, picking up a grand

parts.note: fit means in good health

indicators.note: picking up means taking on board, so the A goes inside the chess word

parts.note: in chess, the knight is famous for forking, attacking two pieces at once

explanation.surface: A fit knight on a chessboard has a special move, and picks up a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like a thousand pounds, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something splendid enough for royalty is grand or magnificent; the idiom praises lavishness.

clue.text: Naughty child loses head — a mistake

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a little terror is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A badly behaved child makes a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a blunder or slip, something done wrongly.

clue.text: Having drunk a sherry ablest drivers may fear these

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are intoxicated and staggered into a new order

explanation.surface: After a sherry, even the most capable motorists might dread being tested by police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as part of the drink-driving story but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices police use to measure alcohol on a motorist's breath, which drink-drivers dread.

clue.text: Crafty May's reset less rigorous schedule for repayment

indicators.note: crafty means artfully reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cunning Theresa May has redrawn a softer plan for paying back debt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a lenient instalment plan for paying off a purchase or loan.

clue.text: Discovers reason to worry when England's batting

definitions.text: reason to worry when England's batting
definitions.meaning: Joe Root was England's star batsman

explanation.surface: Someone finds cause for anxiety while the England cricket team are at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is a leading batsman for England's cricket team; read as 'Root's out' the phrase is bad news for England.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up or unearth, as a pig does, so to find something hidden.

clue.text: Don't put in sir's tooth wonky! They should straighten it out

indicators.note: wonky means crooked or askew, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A plea not to fit a crooked tooth, since specialists should straighten it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' is a link word; the fodder is the letters of Don't, sir's and tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental specialists who correct the alignment of teeth with braces straighten them.

clue.text: In exam clamour to get a first or second perhaps

indicators.note: In placed before both pieces says the noise goes inside the test

parts.note: an oral is a spoken exam
din is a loud clamour

explanation.surface: Despite noise in the exam hall, a student hopes for a first or second-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first or second' suggests degree classes but are examples of a number type.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers like first and second denote position in a sequence, the class this word names.

clue.text: Colonist left bitten by dog

indicators.note: being bitten by puts the letter between the dog's jaws, inside the dog

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gundog

explanation.surface: A pioneer was left bitten by a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a pioneer who makes a home in a new land or colony.

clue.text: Newspaper boss makes investment finally in English fashion house

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the fashion house's name

parts.note: Dior is the famous Paris fashion house

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of investment

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief puts money into an English fashion label.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a newspaper's content is the chief journalist, its head.

clue.text: Note 500 bottles Inland Revenue taxed

indicators.note: bottles means holds inside, as a bottle holds liquid

parts.note: te is a variant of ti, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
IR abbreviates the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A demand from the tax office for 500 pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inland Revenue was Britain's tax authority, now part of HMRC.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxed in the sense of strained or worn out: weary and exhausted.

clue.text: Rascal with Irish accent getting tip-off?

indicators.note: tip-off means the tip, or first letter, comes off

parts.note: a brogue is a strong Irish accent

explanation.surface: A scoundrel with an Irish accent receives a warning from an informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-off' reads as a police informant's warning but means the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a dishonest or mischievous person, a scamp or knave.

clue.text: A new version of Dante to set up with explanations?

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking, so the letters are rearranged
set up also points to the letters being arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: A fresh edition of Dante is to be prepared with notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A text supplied with notes and commentary has been given explanations in its margins.

clue.text: Fine material in newspaper to stop

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical serving a group
to die is to stop, as an engine dies

explanation.surface: Delicate fabric in the paper is being discontinued.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, stiff, transparent muslin used for dresses, hence a fine fabric.

clue.text: Poor nun reaching end of Eucharist gets wine

parts.note: the Poor Clares are an order of nuns, so one is a Clare

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A poverty-stricken nun is given communion wine at the close of mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Clares are a Franciscan order of nuns, so 'Poor' is part of the name, not need.
explanation.definitionFit: The British name for red Bordeaux, a type of wine.

clue.text: Those people acquiring old record for religious study

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the pronoun surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: they means those people
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Some people acquire an old document for their research into religion.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic discipline concerned with God and religious belief, studied at divinity schools.

clue.text: It may delete items from cameras erroneously

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A camera function that wrongly wipes stored photos.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber or pencil-end tool, or a software function, that removes marks or files.
